text: So it's real. And now I have a run I can repeat.
What it reports as observed has to actually be on the page, so it can't just describe the bug back to me.
And the browser it used is already gone.
That sandbox is the same for every run. Point it at a site that loads scripts from all over the place, and you can watch it refuse them.
The page still loads. Anything it isn't allowed to reach gets stopped, and logged.
Okay. Now the part I actually care about: fixing it, and knowing it's fixed.
Rescheduling added a new calendar entry and never moved the old one. Now it moves the one that's already there.
Deployed, and the demo data's back to where it started.
Same bug report, same steps. I'm not changing anything on this side.
That's one path, the way QA hit it. It doesn't mean rescheduling is bug-free. But this one's fixed, and the check's still here, one click away, next time someone touches the calendar.
Which is pretty much what QA asked for in the first place.
